title: Registry.validatePayload never validates against the registered JSON Schema -- ES-05 schema enforcement is a no-op
notes:
Discovered while resolving ISS-0148 (GH #464). TC-ES-05-02 ('append with payload failing registered schema returns PayloadSchemaInvalid') could not be made a real test at EITHER unit or integration level, because the behaviour it asserts does not exist in production code.

src/event_store/registry.zig Registry.validatePayload fetches the registered EventTypeRecord, immediately discards it (`_ = record;`), then performs only a structural is-JSON-object check and returns. It carries an explicit TODO: 'full JSON Schema draft-07 validation against record.json_schema when a JSON Schema validator is available.'

Consequence: ES-05's core acceptance criterion -- 'WHEN a caller appends a payload that fails the registered schema, THEN the platform returns HTTP 422 with an RFC 9457 body listing every validation failure (field path, constraint violated, actual value)' -- is unenforced. Any JSON object payload is accepted for any registered event type regardless of its schema. The ValidationFailure struct and lastValidationFailures() accessor exist but are only ever populated with a single synthetic '/' + 'type' entry for non-object payloads.

This is a production gap, not a test gap. ES-05 is currently marked RELEASED in docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, which overstates its true state.
candidate_resolution: Implement JSON Schema draft-07 validation in Registry.validatePayload against record.json_schema, populating last_failures with one ValidationFailure per violated constraint (field_path as RFC 6901 pointer, constraint keyword, serialised actual value). Then add TC-ES-05-02 as an integration test and re-derive ES-05's status. Note getType() also returns a placeholder record with json_schema hardcoded to '{}' rather than parsing the queried row -- that must be fixed first or schema validation will have nothing real to validate against.
resolution: Fixed both halves of the defect in src/event_store/registry.zig. Registry.getType now parses the queried row into an allocator-owned EventTypeRecord (notably the real stored json_schema) instead of returning a placeholder with json_schema hardcoded to the empty object; a companion freeTypeRecord() releases the owned strings. Registry.validatePayload no longer discards the fetched record -- it delegates to a new pure, DB-free module-level function registry.validatePayloadAgainstSchema(allocator, schema_text, payload), which it itself calls, so unit tests against that function execute production bytes (the ISS-0148 pattern). On non-conformance it returns RegistryError.PayloadValidationFailed (mapped by Store.append to StoreError.PayloadSchemaInvalid) and populates last_failures with ONE ValidationFailure per violated constraint: field_path as an RFC 6901 pointer, constraint as the failing schema keyword, actual as the serialised value -- satisfying ES-05's requirement to list EVERY validation failure. An unparseable STORED schema returns InvalidJsonSchema rather than silently accepting the payload. No new validator was written: the existing src/tools/json_schema.zig (EE-09) was extended with a collecting entry point (validateCollect/deinitViolations/Violation) and the object-structure keywords ES-05's registered schemas use. Validated subset: type, required, properties, items, enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, and additionalProperties:false, applied recursively with RFC 6901 escaping. Explicit non-goals, ignored rather than treated as failures so a schema using them stays permissive: $ref, allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, patternProperties, pattern, format, dependencies, tuple-form items. That subset exactly covers every schema seeded by migrations/002_event_type_registry.sql and migrations/094_entity_subsystem.sql. Build wiring: json_schema.zig is now a NAMED module because registry.zig lives under the event_store module (root store.zig) and cannot reach the validator by relative path; src/main.zig and src/engine/instance.zig were converted to the same named import (a file may belong to exactly one module), and json_schema.zig was given its own b.addTest root wired into test_step so its test blocks continue to execute. Tests: TC-ES-05-02a..g in tests/unit/event_store_test.zig assert BOTH directions (conforming payload accepted; non-conforming rejected with per-field detail), including the ES-05 edge cases, the real seeded ENTITY_RECORD_CREATED schema, an unparseable-stored-schema case, and an explicit ISS-0155 regression guard. TC-ES-05-02 in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig covers the DB half against real PostgreSQL -- that getType returns the STORED schema, not the empty placeholder -- with per-test UUIDs and explicit event-type cleanup. Mutation check performed and passed: disabling validation made TC-ES-05-02b/c/d fail; restoring made them pass. TC-ADP-11-03 had been relying on the broken behaviour (empty-object payload for INSTANCE_STARTED, whose schema requires definition_id); its PAYLOAD was corrected rather than the enforcement weakened. ES-05 remains RELEASED, now honestly: the guarantee it claims exists and is proven in both directions.
prevention: A TODO inside a function that RETURNS SUCCESS is a silent false negative, not a deferral -- the function must either do the work or return an error naming what is missing. This defect survived from 2026-05-21 precisely because every surface signal was right: correct name, correct signature, PayloadValidationFailed present in the error set, a ValidationFailure struct and lastValidationFailures() accessor both defined -- so callers, reviewers and requirement_status.yaml all read as if enforcement existed. It was found only when ISS-0148 tried to WRITE the missing test and discovered the behaviour did not exist; no gate ever detected it. Two concrete practices follow. (1) Before marking a requirement RELEASED, run a mutation check: deliberately break the enforcement and confirm at least one test goes red. A test that passes both with and against the implementation proves nothing, and would have caught this on day one. (2) When a stub returns a PLACEHOLDER for data other code branches on (a schema, a policy, a permission set), that placeholder is more dangerous than a crash -- prefer an explicit error over a permissive default. Also: on finding one stub, grep the whole call chain for siblings before declaring the fix done. Here getType and validatePayload were independently stubbed and mutually masking; repairing either alone would have changed no observable behaviour and produced a confident but false 'fixed'. Recorded in docs/anti-patterns.md under the Agent Workflows table.
